chapter_title: The Interpretation [of] the S[i]lence, the Fast, [

fills.notes: Opening formula introducing a cosmological function; impersonal expository register fits the substrate better than a personal/hagiographic lead-in.
The gatherer is consistently situated in/with the vessel of the Living Waters in this teaching-complex; this also anticipates ¶3’s explicit mention of the ship.
The gatherer’s action is to draw up and cleanse: separating mixed substance from the bodily/erotic influxes (opposite-sense ‘lusts’ as adhesive forces of mixture).
Balances the two sources of bondage just named: bodily impulses and worldly lusts, i.e., internal and external excitations that thicken embodiment.

fills.fill: so that the mixture of the body
fills.notes: Makes explicit the correspondential target: the ‘body’ as the composite plane where mixture occurs; the gatherer acts upon that composite to render it fit for ascent.

fills.fill: the one who bears up the lights
fills.notes: Defines the Pillar’s function in the oldest register: not ‘glory’ as praise but as the luminous supporting axis that carries the separated lights upward through discrete degrees.
Keeps the mechanical/cosmological tone: the Pillar is an instrument of collection and ascent, not a devotional object.
Correspondentially required as the source-region from which ‘lights’ are extracted: the mixed cosmos (world) where lusts and body bind.
Completes the ascent trajectory: the Pillar draws up ‘to the limit’ (boundary) of the upper region, matching Iranian/Manichaean boundary-cosmology without naming later ecclesial terms.

The ‘one they call … it is the First Man’ points to a functional title: the First Man as the steering/intellectual directive within the vessel of Living Waters (guiding the ordered circulation of light).
Keeps the nautical/cosmological correspondence: the First Man ‘dwells’ in the ship and therefore governs its course—an ordering function rather than a salvific sermon.
Restores the expected object after the vessel context: the ship’s content/cargo is ‘light’; the broken trace ‘li]ght’ strongly constrains this.
Old substrate favors functional-intellectual naming: First Man as the luminous Mind/intellect operative within the waters; the broken ‘he is c[alled ...]’ suggests a title phrase with ‘Light’.
Provides the upstream origin of what ‘they have … glorious …’: light/mind is not self-generated in the mixed world but received from the upper boundary/treasury.
Most economical completion for ‘that they have … glorious …’: the ‘powers’ (luminaries/forces) belonging to the First Man’s array; avoids later institutional terms.
Marks a new explanatory unit without introducing dialogue or authority; fits the stripped core style.
Links the act of naming (‘call it day’) to the teachers/knowers as a collective, consistent with impersonal exposition.
Supplies the causal ground for the name ‘day’: day corresponds to illumination (truth made manifest) flowing into the lower expanse.
Completes ‘uni]verse’: ‘whole universe’ is the expected collocation and supports the cosmic scope of the enlightener’s operation.
Balances the later clause ‘it is … established’: describes the fixing of ordered structures in the great aeon after illumination.
Correspondentially: illumination yields order, number, and measure; ‘spread in the universe’ naturally leads to ‘measures’/‘orders’ being established.

fills.fill: are lifted up in their courses
fills.notes: Completes ‘the so[u]ls …’ with the cosmological motion-theme: souls/lights ascend by ordered ‘courses’ once the structures/measures are established; avoids later penitential language.

assessment: Only short fragments are preserved, so most restorations beyond single-letter completions are constrained mainly by the correspondential structure: (1) a ‘gatherer’ who purifies and separates from mixture, (2) the Pillar of Glory as the axial instrument bearing lights upward to a boundary, (3) the First Man as the directing intellect within the ship of Living Waters, and (4) an ‘enlightener’ whose illumination constitutes ‘day’ and establishes cosmic measures and ordered courses. Exact lexical choices remain tentative where the Coptic traces are absent.
